(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili) This Land Acquisition Appeal Suit, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act'), is filed by the State aggrieved by the judgment and decree, dated 09.01.2020, passed in L.A.O.P.No.824 of 2013 by the learned II Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B. Nagar.
2. Cross Objections No.41 of 2021, under Order XLI Rule 22 C.P.C., is filed by the claimants aggrieved by the very same judgment and decree, dated 09.01.2020, seeking enhancement of compensation.
3.

Heard the learned Government Pleader for appeals appearing for the appellants in L.A.A.S.No.83 of 2020 and the respondents in Cross Objections No.41 of 2021 and Sri J. Ashok Kumar, learned counsel for the respondents-claimants in L.A.A.S.No.83 of 2020 and the cross objectors-claimants in Cross Objections No.41 of 2021.
4. For the sake of convenience, the facts and the submissions made in L.A.A.S.No.83 of 2020 are hereunder discussed.

2 AKS,J & RRN,J L.A.A.S.No.83 of 2020 &
5.

Learned Government Pleader for appeals appearing for the appellants had contended that pursuant to the notification, dated 02.03.2012, issued by the appellants, the land admeasuring Ac.0-28  guntas in Survey No.145 situated at Mailardevpally Village, Rajendranagar Mandal,
Ranga Reddy District, belonging to the respondents-claimants was acquired for the purpose of development of P-7 road from Mailardevpally to Srisailam.

The Land Acquisition Officer, after conducting necessary enquiry, has fixed the compensation at Rs.16,50,000/- for the land acquired,
by calculating at the rate of Rs.478.46 ps. per Square Yard, vide Award, dated 03.07.2013.

'the reference Court'), under Section 18 of the Act, seeking enhancement of compensation, by filing the subject L.A.O.P.No.824 of 2013 and the reference Court, vide impugned judgment and decree,
dated 09.01.2020, was pleased to enhance the compensation to Rs.8,625/- per Square Yard with a deduction of 20% of the acquired land for development purpose, without appreciating any of the contentions raised by the appellants.
6.

Learned Government Pleader for appeals appearing for the appellants had further contended that the reference Court ought to 3 AKS,J & RRN,J L.A.A.S.No.83 of 2020 & have deducted 1/3rd for development purpose, but not 20%.

Therefore, appropriate orders be passed in the appeal by setting aside the impugned judgment and decree, dated 09.01.2020.
7.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents had contended that the respondents also filed cross objections seeking enhancement of compensation.

Learned counsel further contended that the land belonging to the respondents is situated on the main road and therefore, the reference Court ought to have awarded compensation of Rs.10,000/- per Square Yard, instead of Rs.8,625/-
per Square Yard.

Learned counsel further contended that the reference Court ought not to have deducted 20% of the acquired land for development purpose, as the land of the respondents was fully developed and it is abutting the main road.

To the said extent, learned counsel for the respondents relied upon the judgment of the Honourable Supreme Court in Trishala Jain and another v. State of Uttaranchal and another 1, wherein the Honourable Supreme Court has held that when once the land is fully developed, the question of deducting any amount from the compensation amount would not arise.

entities.text: Trishala Jain and another v. State of Uttaranchal and another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the amount of compensation determined by the reference Court is erroneous and the reference Court ought to have awarded compensation of Rs.10,000/- per Square Yard, (2011) 6 SCC 47 4 AKS,J & RRN,J L.A.A.S.No.83 of 2020 & without making any deductions, as admittedly, the land of the respondents was fully developed.
Therefore, appropriate orders be passed to that effect.

8. This Court, having considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties,
is of the considered view that the reference Court has taken into account the fact that under Ex.A12- basic register of the S.R.O., the land in Survey No.145 was classified as commercial land with value at Rs.7,500/- per Square Yard as on 10.01.2011 and as there was gap of one year between the said date mentioned in Ex.A12 and the date of acquisition of the subject lands, the reference Court has added 15% towards additional market value to the market value mentioned in Ex.A12, and thereby,
enhanced the compensation from Rs.478.46 ps. per Square Yard, as fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer, to Rs.8,625/- per Square Yard.

Further, as there was no material placed before the reference Court by the respondents to demonstrate that the land acquired was fully developed, the reference Court was justified in deducting 20% for development purpose.
Therefore, the reference Court was justified in enhancing the compensation from Rs.478.46 ps. per Square Yard to Rs.8,625/- per Square Yard, with deduction of 20% for development purpose.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to interfere 5 AKS,J & RRN,J L.A.A.S.No.83 of 2020 & with the impugned judgment and decree.
Therefore, both the appeal and the cross objections are liable to be dismissed.
